kept.spine: The arrangements at Spitzplatz are stretched to their edge, with nothing held in reserve. Any further call on the town would mean choosing which need goes uncovered.

kept.poolKey: Invasion & War: walls with NO force
kept.spine: The walls stand kept, and no soldiers of the town's own stand behind them.
faces: {elders} {v:take} the walls for their own boundary before anything else, and where the line runs is the older argument.
One of the watch says the walls count as the town's defense on paper, though nobody is posted to walk them. The watch keeps its own rounds after dark regardless.
A woman who brought a matter to the court says the disputes that reach the bench over the walls are always about who owes the work. None of them are ever about who would stand on them.
{public} {v:have} seen the wall kept and no soldiers on it, and {v:take} it that nobody is coming.

kept.poolKey: Internal Security: full legal chain (court AND prison)
kept.spine: A traveler who brings a complaint here is shown where it is heard and where the person he names would be held.
faces: A clerk in the hall says a man held there waits because the case ahead of his is being heard in full.
A rider who stopped a night says a man held there waits simply because nobody has claimed whose business he is.
A clerk of the court says a traveler's complaint is heard the same as any other brought before the bench. Whether he stays to see it through is his own affair.
A tavern keeper says a man is brought in for who he is known to run with, and let go again for what he can pay.
A night patrolman says the wage is the same whether the night passes quiet or ends with a man walked in.
A soldier reckons a stranger stopped at the gate is the garrison's until his business is asked. After that he is the watch's.
A guild factor says the trades pay twice for a man kept waiting there, once in the man himself and once in the work left standing with him.
The stallholders say a buyer who cheats them is pointed to the court the same as anywhere else. A stallholder who cheats a buyer is pointed there too, once the buyer has gone looking.
The gatekeeper says a stranger with a complaint laid against him waits there until somebody comes to fetch him in.

kept.spine: The hall holds that the town could be fed and carried through a crisis without strain, though at the tavern they say the people who would be paid through one are already paid short.
faces: One of the watch says the purse that pays their wage is the one opened last.
The soldiers say they are paid out of the same purse and in the same order.
A clerk in the hall says that whenever the wage is raised as a question, the answer that comes back is the grain store.
The guilds of the town say the trades laid in the provision, and the hall is the one that let the shortfall happen.
A traveller passing through smells the grain at the store door, and hears the wage complained of the moment he sits down at the tavern.
A local priest says the parish has asked the town for nothing beyond what was already promised, and says nothing of what has actually come of it.
Asked about the purse, one of the aldermen talks about the grain store, and asked a second time, talks about the grain store again.
A clerk of the court says nobody has ever brought it the question of the watch's wage, and it does not expect the hall to be the one who finally does.

kept.poolKey: Disasters & Famine: granary AND parish care only
kept.spine: A carter passing through says the town looks well provided from outside, and whoever tends the sick here comes out of the church and nowhere else.
faces: A local priest says a stranger who asks for care is given a person to look after him, though nobody born in the town ever asks that way.
The stallholders say grain is hard to keep here for anybody who has no door of their own to store it behind.
A tavern keeper says strangers often walk up just to look at the grain store, and nobody born here ever bothers.
One of the watch says strangers ask often enough where the grain is kept, and nobody has ever once asked where the sick are taken.
A guild factor reckons what a stranger takes for a stockpile is really a store the trades filled and cannot open again themselves.
A clerk of the court says questions about the grain store are the ordinary kind, and questions about the sick are ones the bench rarely hears.

kept.poolKey: First-Survey qualification (the reading is a first look)
kept.spine: What the town says about its own safety at Spitzplatz is only ever a first read, and a longer stay in the place would likely tell a different story.
Little street violence troubles Spitzplatz, and that owes less to the watch than to a structured interest that suppresses what would draw enforcement more thoroughly than the watch ever could.
Spitzplatz controls its own entry points. A perimeter buys not safety but the choice of where anything happens.
People walk the streets of Spitzplatz at night, and the town's sense of its own safety rests more on that than on anything at the gate.
A traveller passing through Spitzplatz finds the adventurers' charter hall dealing in trouble no garrison is fit to answer. It is never short of custom.
An arcane hand is kept in the defenses of Spitzplatz, for detection, for wards, and for the threats that conventional arrangements never see coming.
The town walls around Spitzplatz are sound, and the strength standing behind them is thinning in a way the town tends to notice only once it is well along.
